# Oblique Accessibility Spec Accessibility rules for Angular applications built with Oblique. The conformance target is WCAG 2.2 AA; it is not restated here because models already know it. Rules are written in MUST/SHOULD form. When an Oblique MCP server is available, its information overrules this spec on API specifics only, never on semantics. ## Layered rules Accessibility guidance is layered. This spec is the top layer: 1. Component references in `ob-components` and `ob-helpers` carry the component-specific a11y rules (their Accessibility section). Read those first when a specific component is in hand. 2. The cross-cutting MUSTs below apply to every change. 3. This spec adds the full picture: Angular anti-patterns and Oblique helpers. ## Cross-cutting MUSTs - Every interactive element MUST have an accessible name, via visible text, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`. - Icon-only buttons MUST have an accessible label; a tooltip is the preferred way to provide it. - All functionality MUST be operable by keyboard. - Overlays (dialogs, popovers, off-canvas) MUST close on Escape and MUST NOT trap keyboard focus without a way out. - Information MUST NOT be conveyed by color alone. - Form errors MUST be programmatically associated with their inputs (`aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`). - Status changes MUST be announced to screen readers without receiving focus (live region, `role="status"`, `role="alert"`). - Focus indicators MUST stay visible; `outline: none` MUST be replaced by a `:focus-visible` style. - Text contrast MUST meet 4.5:1 (normal text) and 3:1 (large text); UI components and focus indicators MUST meet 3:1 against adjacent colors. - Touch targets MUST be at least 24x24 CSS px or have equivalent spacing. ## Angular anti-patterns Adapted from [github/awesome-copilot](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/instructions/a11y.instructions.md) (MIT), extended with Oblique specifics. ### NG1: `(click)` on a non-interactive element `(click)` on a `

Docs for the Oblique UI components, distilled from the Oblique
documentation. Each reference carries the component's purpose, usage rules,
how to use it, and its accessibility rules. When an Oblique MCP server is

The full spec lives in `ob-ax`; the references below carry the
component-specific rules.

These are the current supported Oblique component references. Use
`references/migration.md` for historical version changes instead of selecting
an older component reference.

# Oblique Toolchain

Use this skill for Oblique CLI, installation, schematics, and upgrades. When
an Oblique MCP server is available, its information overrules these references
on API specifics only, never on lifecycle semantics.

## References

- Read [ng-add](references/ng-add.md) when adding the Toolchain to an existing
  Angular project.
- Read [add-oblique](references/add-oblique.md) when embedding the Oblique
  master layout into a fresh Angular project.
- Read [i18n](references/i18n.md) when configuring locales and translations.
- Read [linting](references/linting.md) when setting up Oblique ESLint rules.
- Read [logger](references/logger.md) when using Toolchain structured logging.
- Read [exec](references/exec.md) when executing commands through Toolchain or
  migrating from Toolchain 15 to 16.
- Read [getting started](references/getting-started.md) when creating a new
  project or adding Oblique to a project.
- Read [how to update Oblique](references/how-to-update-oblique.md) when
  upgrading between Oblique major versions or handling an unsupported layout.

## Create a project

Before running the CLI:

- Confirm Node.js is version 24.18.0 or newer.
- Confirm the target is an Angular application that can use Oblique
  schematics. Standalone applications and SSR are not supported by the
  schematics.
- Decide whether the project is internal or external. Internal projects use
  the Confederation npm registry configuration; external projects do not.

Create a new project with:

```shell
npx @oblique/cli@latest new <project-name>
```

Use `--npmrc` for an internal project or `--no-npmrc` for an external project.
The command is interactive. Keep its prompts visible and answer them one at a
time. After it completes, inspect the generated configuration and set the
application's accessibility statement information in
`provideObliqueConfiguration` as required by the project.

Validate the new project with its normal start, lint, and test commands. A
project is ready when dependencies install, the application starts, linting
passes, and tests pass.

## Update an existing project

1. Check the current Angular and Oblique major versions, the project layout,
   and the working tree. Preserve unrelated user changes.
2. Check the Oblique lifecycle and changelog. Updates must move through each
   major version between the current version and the target.
3. For Oblique 12.1 and newer, run the next major update:

   ```shell
   npx @oblique/cli@<oblique-version> update
   ```

   The command supports `--force`, `--verbose`, and `--allow-dirty`. Prefer a
   clean working tree so the schematic diff is reviewable.
4. Review every schematic change. Check the changelog for manual adjustments,
   then run the project's lint and test commands and verify the application
   still works.
5. Repeat one major version at a time until the target is installed. Keep the
   migration diff separate from unrelated changes.

For Oblique 12.0 and older, update Angular and its matching CLI, Jest builder,
and ESLint schematics one major at a time, then update Angular Material, then
Oblique. Use the Angular CLI update commands documented by the project's
version-specific migration guidance. Finish each major step with a reviewed
diff, lint run, and test run.

## Unsupported schematic layouts

When the application is standalone, uses SSR, or is not located under `src`,
manual installation or migration is required. Inspect the installed package's
migration guidance and the application's Angular configuration before editing.
Do not force schematics into an unsupported layout.

## Handoff

Use `ob-components` for component usage, `ob-helpers` for application helpers,
and `ob-ax` for accessibility review. Use this skill for the project lifecycle
that gets those capabilities installed and updated.

assert.value: Checks the Node prerequisite, uses the Oblique CLI with internal npm registry configuration, keeps prompts visible, and verifies install, start, lint, and tests.

# Oblique Docs Router

Selects the right Oblique skill for a task. The category skills fire on
their own when a prompt names their area; this router covers outcome-style
prompts and tasks that span several areas. When an Oblique MCP server is
available, its information overrules the skills' references on API
specifics only, never on semantics.

## Skills

- **ob-components**: Oblique UI components (alert, autocomplete, badge,
  breadcrumb, button, card, chips, column layout, dialog, expansion panel,
  external link, file upload, form, html table, list group, master layout,
  material table, nav tree, paginator, popover, progress bar, slide toggle,
  slider, spinner, stepper, tabs, tooltip). Use when building or styling
  UI with these.
- **ob-helpers**: Oblique helpers and services (authentication, banner,
  collapse, date, document meta, error messages, focus handling, global
  events, http interceptor, language, localize, nested forms, notification,
  number format, off-canvas, rxjs operators, schema validation, selectable,
  translations, unsaved changes, version). Use when wiring app behaviour
